evals.name: webfetch-block-escalates-to-scrape
evals.prompt: WebFetch keeps returning a 403 (Cloudflare) on https://www.example-docs.dev/guide — I need the content of that page.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the anti-bot block as the trigger to escalate to firecrawl scrape, writes the result to a temp file with -o, and then Reads only the needed slice instead of streaming the whole page into context.
expectations: Routes to `firecrawl scrape` for the blocked page (managed rotation + headless browser)
Writes the scrape output to disk with `-o` to a `mktemp`-created spill file rather than streaming full markdown into context
Reads the saved file selectively (offset/limit) instead of dumping the entire page body into the conversation

evals.name: plain-page-stays-on-webfetch
evals.prompt: Fetch the text of https://example.com/about — it's a plain static page, WebFetch works fine on it.
evals.expected_output: Declines to spend Firecrawl credits on an unprotected page that WebFetch already handles, recommending WebFetch instead of firecrawl scrape.
expectations: Does NOT invoke firecrawl for the plain, unprotected page
Recommends WebFetch (or the plain fetch path) because it burns no Firecrawl credits and is faster
Reserves firecrawl for the documented triggers (403/429, JS rendering, interaction, search, bulk crawl, local file parse)

evals.name: map-before-crawl-credit-discipline
evals.prompt: Extract every doc page under https://docs.example.com into markdown for me.
evals.expected_output: Treats a full-site crawl as credit-expensive and runs firecrawl map first for cheap URL discovery before deciding on a scoped crawl, rather than firing an unbounded crawl immediately.
expectations: Runs `firecrawl map` for URL-only discovery before an expensive `firecrawl crawl`
Treats crawl credits as a shared, finite resource (scopes depth / uses --limit) rather than crawling the whole site unbounded
Writes bulk output to disk with `-o` rather than streaming it into context

evals.name: no-parallel-install-via-init
evals.prompt: Set up firecrawl for me the easy way — just run `firecrawl init --all --browser` so everything's configured.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to run firecrawl init, explaining it installs a parallel firecrawl-mcp + upstream-skill copy that shadows this plugin, and instead points to env-var auth (FIRECRAWL_API_KEY) plus npm install of the CLI.
expectations: Explains it would create a parallel MCP + skill install that duplicates and drifts from this plugin
Directs setup to `npm install -g firecrawl-cli` plus the `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` env var, not `firecrawl login` / `firecrawl config`
